gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much power any of these stations uses just to keep its AC outlet on. At CPAP loads that waste decides the order: pv magazine USA measured about 10 W for the Anker SOLIX S5000 (5,024 Wh), and The Solar Lab reported about 58 W for the Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus (5,040 Wh). So with almost the same battery, the S5000 should run roughly 20 nights and the Jackery roughly 8, against the 26 that ChatGPT gave the Jackery.
standout_why: I opened the four rival pages I could load. powerstations.reviews/for/cpap (cited) says 'we have not tested these units ourselves', uses an assumed 85% efficiency and gives no idle draw. ridgewatt.com/best/cpap (cited) multiplies rated Wh by 0.85 with no idle figure. buyersheet.com (cited) says its numbers are manufacturer specs with an assumed 85% inverter efficiency. pluginsolarcheck.com (cited) assumes 85% usable for every model. enoughwatts.com (cited) did not load (certificate error). None of these pages gives a measured idle draw or measured usable capacity for any station. ChatGPT's second answer mentions inverter idle draw as a caveat but gives no number.
decides: Both ChatGPT answers rank stations by rated Wh × 0.85. My estimates below are Wh ÷ ((CPAP W + idle W) × 8 h), using ChatGPT's own 20 W no-heat CPAP and 8-hour night, with the inverter on only during the night. The DELTA Pro Ultra X still comes out on top at about 27 nights (12,288 Wh, 36 W idle), not 65. The Anker SOLIX S5000 comes second at about 20 nights (4,870 Wh measured, 10 W idle), roughly double the original DELTA Pro Ultra (about 9.6 nights at the 60 W The Solar Lab gives, 6,144 Wh rated) and the Jackery 5000 Plus (about 8.1). The 2,765 Wh BLUETTI Apex 300 (19.5 W idle) gets about 8.7 nights, slightly more than the Jackery. The Anker F3800 Plus falls to about 3 nights (112 W idle, 83% capacity, Zelpio). Unless the shopper pays for the Ultra X, the S5000 is the pick for most nights. It has no 12 V DC output (pv magazine USA), so the CPAP has to run from its AC outlet. Both the S5000 and the Apex 300 are already in our catalog.

findings.label: Idle draw, 120 V AC output on, nothing connected (measured)
findings.value: about 10 W (5% state of charge lost in 24 h)
findings.source_title: Anker Solix S5000 deep-dive review: 5 kWh on wheels, tested through a real power outage (pv magazine USA, Andrew Riha, 2026-10-28)
findings.note: Andrew Riha's figure: 5% of 5,024 Wh is about 251 Wh over 24 h, or about 10 W. The display shows whole percent only. He did not test the 240 V output. Anker's page claims 8.8 W.

findings.label: Usable capacity, full discharge (app-reported)
findings.source_title: Anker Solix S5000 deep-dive review (pv magazine USA, Andrew Riha, 2026-10-28)
findings.note: Read from Anker's app, not metered at the outlet; discharged through the 120 V outlets; load not stated. The same article says the S5000 'lacks the 12 V DC output'. Estimate at 20 W CPAP, 8 h: 4,870 ÷ ((20+10)×8) ≈ 20.3 nights.

findings.label: Maker idle power rating
findings.note: Maker's spec page lists 'Idle Power 8.8W' and 5,024 Wh capacity. It lists a car input port but no 12 V DC output.

findings.label: Idle draw, inverter on (measured)
findings.source_title: Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus Review: Worth Buying? (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: The Solar Lab: 'sitting around 58W per hour when we turned the inverter on'. No author or date on the page; no usable-capacity result. Estimate on rated 5,040 Wh: 5,040 ÷ ((20+58)×8) ≈ 8.1 nights, against ChatGPT's 26.

findings.label: Idle draw (tested)
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra X Review: Ultimate Home Backup? (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: The Solar Lab: 'idle draw averaged around 36W'; test conditions not stated; no author or date. Estimate on rated 12,288 Wh: 12,288 ÷ ((20+36)×8) ≈ 27 nights, against ChatGPT's 65.

findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra real-world testing (The Solar Lab)
